Most mobile chat tutorials rely on Firebase or third-party cloud SDKs.

I decided to build a full-stack WhatsApp alternative completely from scratch — sub-50ms latency, zero Firebase, and verified cross-platform parity on Apple iOS and Google Android. ⚡

During my Mobile Application Development (HHDP 1) module, I built Tappsy: pairing the proven UX patterns of WhatsApp (Chats/Updates/Calls tabs, speech bubbles with directional tails, double blue ticks ✓✓, status story rings) with an electric brand identity (#0084FF).

💡 Key Engineering Highlights:
• Instant Sub-50ms Messaging: Bidirectional WebSockets (wss://) hosted on a native Java EE / Jakarta EE server (@ServerEndpoint), eliminating polling overhead and conserving mobile battery life.
• Resilient Socket Engine: Custom client-side heartbeat loop (Ping/Pong) with exponential backoff to handle mobile network handovers cleanly.
• Dual-Theme Parity: Complete Light (#FFFFFF) and Dark Mode (#0F172A Slate) styling dynamically syncing with system appearance via custom ThemeProvider & NativeWind.
• End-to-End Onboarding: Animated flow with country-code dialing (+94 Sri Lanka defaults), SHA-256 PIN security, and multipart avatar uploads.
• Dual-Platform Verification: Captured live on both Apple iOS Simulator (iPhone 18 Pro) and Google Android Emulator (Pixel 9a).

Swipe through the clean presentation deck below to see the side-by-side iOS vs. Android comparisons and architectural deep dive! 📱👉

Which theme looks cleaner to you: Light Mode or Dark Mode? Let me know in the comments! 👇

posts.text:
One of the fastest ways to trigger a React hydration mismatch in a Next.js App Router application is a single line of date formatting code.

Everything looks completely normal on your local machine. Then you deploy to production, and the browser console throws a hydration error while dates briefly flicker on mobile screens.

Here is why it happens:
Your Next.js Server Component renders the HTML on a Vercel server running in UTC time. When the user opens the page in Jakarta, Sydney, or London, their browser runs client-side hydration using their local timezone and locale settings.

If your component calls new Date().toLocaleDateString() directly during render, the server output and the browser output do not match. React rejects the mismatch and forces an expensive client re-render.

Here are three clean ways we eliminate timezone hydration bugs in production:

1. Lock the Timezone Explicitly on Both Sides:
Never rely on implicit default locales inside Intl.DateTimeFormat or toLocaleDateString. Pass both the locale and an explicit timeZone parameter (for example, 'en-US' and 'UTC' or a stored user timezone preference from the database) so the server and browser produce the exact same string.

2. Defer Local User Timezone Formatting Until Mount:
If you genuinely need the visitor's local browser clock (like "2 hours ago" or local event times), render a deterministic fallback or ISO date on the server, then update to the local string inside a small isolated client wrapper after mount. Never wrap an entire page in a mounted check just to format a timestamp.

3. Pass Serialized ISO Strings Across Server-Client Boundaries:
Pass plain ISO strings from Server Components into Client Components instead of raw Date instances or pre-formatted strings that drop timezone offsets.

Hydration bugs rarely come from complicated business logic. Nine times out of ten, they come from small assumptions about browser globals like window, Date, or invalid nested HTML tags.

What is the trickiest Next.js hydration bug you have had to track down in production?

SUSTAINABILITY DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY CREATE GUEST TRUST — OR HOTEL INVESTMENT VALUE.

An important new study by Siregar, Tjahjono and Santamaria (2026), published in the Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management, examines 81 academic studies to understand how hotels' environmental claims influence guest trust before booking.

Five factors emerge: tangible evidence, transparency, credible certification, environmental reputation and alignment with guests' personal values.

For Bali and Indonesia, the implications extend beyond hotel marketing: sustainability credentials must be supported by actual operating practices, while a property's environmental reputation increasingly needs to be considered within the broader destination experience.

For hotel owners, developers and investors, I believe the more important question is whether sustainability can create measurable competitive advantage through stronger booking preference, improved operating efficiency and reduced investment risk.

The research provides a useful conceptual foundation, although it does not establish the financial returns associated with these relationships.

My perspective: the next frontier is moving from sustainability claims to evidence-based sustainability performance — and from guest trust to demonstrable business value.

This also reinforces the importance of Homeostatic Tourism, where hotels, communities and destinations adapt their strategies in response to measurable environmental, social and economic conditions.

Are we investing sufficiently in sustainability outcomes, or are we investing too heavily in communicating them?

Source: Siregar, G. S., Tjahjono, B., & Santamaria, D. (2026). From green claims to guest trust. Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management. https://lnkd.in/eZPEDfCh

Inverto Earth, led by CEO Dr. Jürg Germann, raised $2.4M: a Seed round led by Bloom Foundation, to build a restoration intelligence platform for coastal ecosystems.

Mangroves, saltmarshes and seagrass protect coastlines and store carbon, but restoring them is slow, costly and risky. Inverto Earth combines ecohydrology, robotics and digital monitoring to help project developers pick the right sites, plant at scale and verify results. Its patent-pending Seed Darts anchor mangrove seeds directly into the soil, planted by hand or from drones. The founders first built drone systems for UN mosquito-control programmes before pivoting to coastal restoration. It works on projects across Pakistan, Senegal, Saudi Arabia and Indonesia, with partners including Delta Blue Carbon, WWF and Universitas Gadjah Mada. The round connects site selection and monitoring with field hardware such as robotic planting systems and sensors. Zürcher Kantonalbank, Venture Kick, Kickfund, Techstars, Valery Foundation and SICTIC angels joined, with Innosuisse providing public innovation funding.

posts.text:
The US spent months figuring out how to keep China away from American chips. Chinese labs, meanwhile, just asked ChatGPT and trained on its answers. OpenAI's rules forbid this; the law doesn't.

On November 16, the US Commerce Department closed an old loophole. Chinese companies have long been banned from buying advanced Nvidia chips, but could rent them in a data center in Singapore or Malaysia and work remotely. Now any data center anywhere that leases Chinese customers a lot of that compute needs a US license — for the law, renting is now the same as exporting. Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil now need Washington's permission just to buy these chips at all.

The trigger was the Nvidia scandal: Singapore's Megaspeed bought about $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over three years, and investigators believe it used shell companies to grant access to 240,000 chips banned from export to China. The company denies everything. The affair ended with Jensen Huang's resignation. A similar rule had been blocked by Commerce Secretary Lutnick back in summer 2025, and was only adopted after the resignation.

That same day, Reuters published an investigation based on more than 300 Chinese papers, patents, and job listings. The conclusion: in China it's become standard practice to take American models' answers and train on them — "distillation" — with dedicated software and hired staff now built around it. A Shanghai university turned about 5,000 OpenAI model answers into training data for an Alibaba model. Alibaba itself has described generating data via GPT-4. Meituan, the Chinese food-delivery service, trained its models on GPT-4o. In January, eight Chinese ministries issued a state program explicitly backing distillation as a way to cut AI costs.

A US official told Reuters that Washington sees this as the main reason Chinese models have nearly caught up with American ones. People familiar with Chinese developers' work disagree, calling it one factor among many, alongside engineering and data. Anthropic says it recently learned to block most such attempts.

One more detail: the same rule also scrapped the Biden-era export controls on trained models themselves. Chips are now guarded by licenses worldwide, but their output is still freely available through any chat window.

For the average user, the takeaway is simple: cheap Chinese models that are "almost like Claude at a third of the price" are partly cheap because they trained on American answers. The investigation's examples span 2024–2026 models, and the rental rule is still temporary — it's open for public comment for another 60 days.

There are multiple initiatives taking place around AI agents, plus concerns over the leadership patterns of large organisations that throw the premise of diligent, thorough, and effective leadership into question. On a brighter note, the SME market in the UK is showing some rates of improvement. To finish off, I've included a rather relevant video that covers the AI usage in the UK.
- IBM's new Chief AI Officer study finds 75% say governance, risk or compliance delays AI-driven action, even as 48% report AI agents already initiating and executing workflow actions on their own
- Gartner: 74% of organisations expect to deploy agentic AI within 12 months, but only 14% of Asia-Pacific CIOs have governance ready — Gartner is warning AI risk is growing faster than business value as firms rush in
- The UK Pensions Regulator published new guidance for trustees on responsible AI use, built around a low/medium/high risk-based approach rather than new rules.
- The EU is piloting a rights-impact-assessment questionnaire for high-risk AI systems under Article 27 of the AI Act
- The US is closing a chip-export loophole, requiring licences for shipments to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, to stop Chinese firms accessing advanced chips via third-country data centres; Reuters separately reports Chinese firms increasingly "distilling" US models to train domestic rivals
- The AI trade wobbled further as Anthropic heads toward an IPO reportedly eyeing a $1.5 trillion valuation, down from $2 trillion expected just weeks ago; Nvidia fell again on the export-control news
- A government-commissioned Access to Banking Review could force digital-only banks like Monzo and Revolut to help fund face-to-face banking services for the roughly 3 million people who still rely on branches
- Revolut's Italian arm was placed under one-year judicial administration over anti-money-laundering control concerns; not a criminal probe, and it must submit an action plan within 60 days
- DDI's Global Leadership Forecast 2027, surveying over 11,000 leaders, finds only 25% say their manager coaches them effectively
- HBR examines why CEOs wait too long to shake up underperforming leadership teams, using Netflix's recent content-chief change as the case study
- Wharton's Peter Cappelli argues companies have largely abandoned structured management-development pipelines, which is part of why engineer-led firms can make riskier leadership calls
- iwoca's SME Expert Index shows UK small businesses swinging back to growth: hiring-cut reports have halved since Q2, and two-thirds of advisers expect SME finance demand to rise over the next six months
- From April 2027, young side-hustlers and freelancers get a tripled tax-free trading allowance, up to £3,000

And here's that video.....

In this informative 30-minute session, you'll learn how profile rail guides support precise linear movement in industries ranging from machine tools and packaging equipment to medical technology and industrial automation. Cindy will explain the fundamentals of profile rail guide design, explore the advantages of KLLT's unique X-arrangement, and demonstrate how its self-aligning characteristics can help compensate for installation and mounting misalignments.

Drawing on her extensive application expertise, Cindy will also highlight the many enhancements that distinguish the KLLT from its predecessor, including optimized ball recirculation for smoother running behavior, advanced sealing technology that significantly reduces friction, multiple lubrication options for easier maintenance, and a redesigned lubrication system that can reduce grease consumption while supporting longer service intervals.

Whether you're designing new equipment, upgrading existing systems, or evaluating alternatives for linear motion applications, this webinar will provide practical insights into selecting and applying profile rail guides for improved performance, reliability, and ease of maintenance. If you're looking for a robust, smooth-running, and cost-effective linear guidance solution, this is one webinar you won't want to miss!

Two weeks in Southeast Asia. A clearer view of what’s next for SANS SOUCI.

Singapore → Kuala Lumpur → Jakarta → back to Singapore.

Over the past two weeks, I met with local partners, interior designers, developers, architects and our Asia team. As Chief Sales Officer, I value time on the ground. It helps me make better decisions about where to invest, which partnerships to deepen and how best to support our team in the region.

The trip reinforced something I’ve long believed. In a global business, relationships grow through collaboration across markets. A conversation in Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Jakarta or Bangkok can lead to a project anywhere in the world.

Our next steps will soon take shape, starting with a new SANS SOUCI showroom in Singapore. We’re creating an experience centre where designers and local partners can see our lighting firsthand and collaborate with our team.

Thank you to everyone who made time to meet with me, and to our Asia team for building these relationships every day.

📢 WE ARE HIRING: Senior Penetration Tester
 
 
Hello Job Seekers!

I’m Muhammad Hafizh, Tech Recruiter from PT. MSBU Konsultan Indonesia. We are currently looking for one person to join as a Senior Penetration Tester of our client companies for Information Technology Sector Industry in Location DKI Jakarta Area and 12 month Employment Contract.
 
Job Description:
-   Lead technical scoping, establish Rules of Engagement (RoE) with stakeholder and execute end-to-end assessment independently
-   Perform deep dive assessment on Web, Mobile (Android/iOS), API (REST/GraphQL), Network, Active Directory, and Cloud/Container environments with manual validation to eliminate false positives
-   Produce clear, two-tiered report consisting of an Executive Summary for leadership and reproducible technical details with prioritized remediation steps for developer
-   Lead debrief session, presenting complex technical finding effectively to both non-technical business leader and technical engineering team
-   Conduct retest to verify fix effectiveness and ensure long-term risk mitigation
-   Drive continuous improvement by building internal tooling, refining checklist/playbook and mentoring junior team member
 
 
Requirement:
-   Minimum 4 years of experience in offensive security or 7 years in general cybersecurity with at least 4 years exclusively focus on penetration testing, experience bug bounty.
-   Proven experience independently managing critical engagement within high-risk sector (Financial Services, Telecommunication, E-Commerce or Government)
-   In-depth knowledge of OWASP Top 10 and WSTG. Expertise in testing authentication/authorization flaws, IDOR, SSRF, insecure deserialization, business logic bugs, and API vulnerabilities (REST & GraphQL batching/introspection abuse)
-  Deep knowledge of OWASP MASTG, Hands on experience with static/dynamic analysis on Android & iOS, including client-side security bypasses
-  Proficient in Python, Bash or PowerShell (Go or C# is a plus).
-  Familiar with PTES, OSSTMM, NIST SP 800-115, MITRE ATT&CK, CVSS v3.1/v4.0, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, as well as Indonesian regulation (POJK/SEOJK and UU PDP)
-  Preferred Certification (Practical/Hands-on): OSCP (Primary), paired with OSEP, OSWE, GPEN, GWAPT, CRTO or CREST CRT
-  Bonus / Advanced: OSCE³, GXPN, CARTP/CARTS, eWPTX, or GMOB
-  Complementary: CEH, CompTIA PenTest+
